title: Extension by zero through the schematic closure
statement:
In the situation of [det-nagata-density-normalization-setup], let
$\Lambda$ be a condensed coefficient ring with pulled-back coefficient
sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Z,\Lambda_{\overline X}$. For every sheaf $M$ of
$\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}$ the unit
$\eta:j_!M\to i_*i^*j_!M$ of $i^*\dashv i_*$ is an isomorphism, and the
base-change isomorphism $i^*j_!M\simeq j_{Z,!}M$ identifies it with a natural
isomorphism

$$
j_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }i_*j_{Z,!}M .
$$

Consequently, for every complex $K$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules (unbounded), the
same map, applied degreewise, is an isomorphism of complexes
$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$, and it induces the identification
$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$ in $D(\overline X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_{\overline X})$.

proof.text:
The setup gives $\overline X$ and $Z$ qcqs, $V$ an open with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$, and $j_Z:X\hookrightarrow Z$ a quasi-compact open immersion. Quasi-compactness of the morphisms $j_V$ and $j$ is checked as follows. For an affine open $A\subseteq\overline X$, [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies $j_V^{-1}(A)$ and $j^{-1}(A)$ with the open subsets $V\cap A$ and $j(X)\cap A$ of the Noetherian scheme $\overline X$; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes these opens quasi-compact, and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] then gives that $j_V$ and $j$ are quasi-compact. We read “condensed coefficient ring” in the module-object statement in the commutative sense required by [def-sfb-module-upper-star], [def-sfb-module-lower-star] and [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]; this is the standing coefficient convention and adds no geometric hypothesis. The hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] hold for $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, $T\in\{X,Z,V,\overline X\}$: the site is formed inside the universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with a small skeleton, and [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] gives abelian sheafification $a$ as a strong symmetric monoidal functor for the sheafified tensor product, so $a(g\otimes_p h)$ is invertible whenever $a(g)$ and $a(h)$ are (local equivalences are monoidal); $\Lambda_T$ is a commutative monoid by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Hence, by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], internal modules over the commutative ring object $Λ_T$ are equivalent to sectionwise module sheaves, preserving underlying abelian sheaves, sections, restrictions, and linear maps. Under this equivalence, [def-sfb-module-upper-star] is the ringed inverse image (its scalar extension is along the coefficient isomorphism $α_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]), [def-sfb-module-lower-star] is the sectionwise direct image, and [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] is the abelian-sheaf extension by zero with its transported module action. The adjunctions are the actual module adjunctions by [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Therefore [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1)--(3), applied on $\overline X$ to $(j_V,i)$ and to $j$ with its closed complement, and on the qcqs scheme $Z$ to $j_Z$ with its closed complement, transports to the internal module categories and gives exact $i_*,j_!,j_{Z,!}$ and the exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_{V,!}j_V^*N\longrightarrow N\xrightarrow{\eta_N}i_*i^*N\longrightarrow0.$$ The exactness of the internal $i^*$ is the transported assertion of [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits](2). The transported sequence map is the unit of the module adjunction, since both its underlying sheaf map and its module linearity are the canonical unit maps just identified.

The square with top arrow $\mathrm{id}_X$, bottom arrow $i:Z\to\overline X$, and vertical arrows $j_Z,j$ is cartesian by setup clause (3). In the sectionwise module category, clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives $i^*j_!\cong j_{Z,!}$ because $Z$ is qcqs. The equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], together with the coefficient-isomorphism transport in [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and the module adjunction of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], carries this natural transformation to the internal-module pullback and the internal extensions by zero. Hence the resulting canonical isomorphism is the module isomorphism $\beta_M:i^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{Z,!}M$, natural in $M$.

The setup gives $X\times_{\overline X}V=\varnothing$, and $V$ is qcqs because it is a quasi-compact open of the quasi-separated scheme $\overline X$. Apply clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] to $g=j_V$ and the open immersion $j$. The pullback open is the empty scheme, so the sectionwise extension by zero is the zero module sheaf. Through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and the definition of $j_!$ in [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], this identifies the actual internal pullback $j_V^*j_!M$ with the zero internal module.

Apply the internal-module exact sequence from Step 1 to $N=j_!M$. Step 3 makes its first term zero, so $0\to j_!M\xrightarrow{\eta_M}i_*i^*j_!M\to0$. The category of sectionwise module sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is abelian, and the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] makes the internal category $\Mod_{\Lambda_{\overline X}}$ abelian with exact sequences corresponding (an equivalence of additive categories preserves kernels and cokernels); hence this unit is a monomorphism and an epimorphism in an abelian category, i.e. an isomorphism. It is the specified unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$ by the identification in Step 1, rather than a unit from a different sectionwise adjunction. Composing it with $i_*\beta_M$ gives the required natural isomorphism $j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*j_{Z,!}M$.

For an arbitrary integer-indexed complex $K$, apply the natural isomorphism $\theta=i_*\beta\circ\eta$ in each degree. Naturality gives $\theta_{K^{n+1}}j_!(d^n)=i_*j_{Z,!}(d^n)\theta_{K^n}$; multiplying by the inverse components shows that the inverses also commute with differentials, so this is an isomorphism of complexes. The functors are exact by Step 1, hence preserve quasi-isomorphisms by the elementary homology calculation $H^n(FC)\cong F(H^nC)$. The chain isomorphism therefore descends through the localization defining the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], giving $j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$ in the asserted derived category.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned E6/C1 fault by routing every operation through the internal module-object category: added the actual module functor definitions, adjunction, lower-shriek definition, internal/sectionwise equivalence, and internal abelianness to the statement and proof dependencies; explicitly matched pullback, pushforward, extension by zero, base-change maps, and the unit. Settled the required commutativity convention openly (the module-object operations used here are defined for commutative condensed rings). Corrected the setup quasi-compactness attribution and retained the Noetherian-open argument. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the five steps in det-nagata-density-normalization-sheaves.proof.md: exact operations, base change, vanishing on V, sheaf conclusion, and degreewise complexes.

tool_uses.why: Generic arbitrary-ring sectionwise open–closed exactness and base-change theorem; after the explicitly cited internal/sectionwise module equivalence and module-operation definitions, it supplies the transported exact sequence and base-change used here.

Generic equivalence transports the sectionwise open–closed theorem to the internal module-object category and preserves the underlying maps, so it is needed to identify the actual module operations and unit.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-3d56f0d6a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof (Steps 1-5), the unit sk-lem-nagata-density-normalization and the unit sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle, and the statement of every cited node (none has a blueprint_update). The statement matches the blueprint word for word and is not weakened. It uses the internal Mod_{Λ_T} coefficient category, and the base change β_M comes from the cartesian square of setup clause (3). 'Condensed ring' is commutative under the Stacks sheaf-of-rings convention, and the module functors that the statement uses require it. Steps 2, 3 and 5 are correct. Step 2 applies clause (4) of det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf with g=i, Z qcqs and U'=X. Step 3 uses g=j_V with an empty pullback open. Step 5 is a degreewise chain isomorphism followed by the localization Q. I repaired three small faults in the corrected item file. (1) Step 1 claimed j_V is quasi-compact 'by definition'; the Noetherian-open argument now covers j_V as well as j, and the meaningless pair (j,j_Z) is replaced by j on X̄ and j_Z on qcqs Z, each with its closed complement. (2) The hypotheses of the internal/sectionwise equivalence were never checked; Step 1 now cites def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure and sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients for them. (3) Step 4 cited lem-sfb-modobj-abelian without checking its hypotheses, and that lemma is off-route and was undeclared; abelianness now comes from def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category transported along the equivalence. proof_deps is updated to the union of the step uses; the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Accepted tool_uses: det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf, because the route's open-closed unit is étale, D_ctf and finite-type only, and def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence, which is an interface definition. No new nodes and no duplicates (det-nagata-density-normalization-pushforward cites the item; the condensed recollement node is D^+ only with no base change). No cycle and no SGA. Edge cases checked: X empty, X = X̄, a disjoint extra component, a non-reduced closure with V empty, and Λ = 0.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
